title: YouTube Video Platform: Complete Architecture
description: Design a YouTube-like video streaming platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a video streaming platform like YouTube. Users upload videos that are transcoded into multiple bitrates for adaptive streaming, browse recommendations, like and comment, subscribe to channels, and watch live streams. The system must handle 500 hours of video uploaded every minute and serve billions of streams daily with sub-3s time-to-first-frame.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Upload videos via chunked/resumable upload for files up to 128GB
Transcode uploaded videos into multiple bitrates (144p to 4K) and codecs (H.264, VP9, AV1)
Adaptive bitrate streaming (HLS/DASH) with automatic quality switching based on bandwidth
Video player with playback controls, captions/subtitles, quality selector, and playback speed
Like, dislike, comment, and share videos with threaded replies
Subscribe to channels with notification preferences (all, personalized, none)
Personalized home feed and recommendations based on watch history and engagement
Live streaming with sub-second latency and real-time chat overlay
Playlist management: create, reorder, public/private, collaborative playlists
Content ID system to detect copyrighted material and claim/ad monetize
Video chapters, end screens, and cards for creator engagement
Age-restricted content gating and regional availability controls

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Sub-3s time-to-first-frame for video playback globally
99.99% streaming availability with multi-CDN failover
Support 500+ hours of video uploaded per minute with parallel transcoding
Transcoding latency under 30 minutes for 4K content
Global CDN with 200+ edge locations for cache-hit ratio above 95%
Adaptive streaming resilience: switch quality within 2 seconds of bandwidth drop
Live stream latency under 5 seconds for主播-to-viewer path
DRM support for premium content (Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady)
Immutable audit logs for Content ID claims and copyright disputes

data.text: Build a monolithic ASP.NET Core API with SQL Server. Use FFmpeg for local transcoding during upload, store originals in Azure Blob Storage, and serve via Azure CDN. Implement SQL-based recommendations using watch history joins. This validates the upload-to-playback pipeline and basic metadata management.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API with clean architecture
  - Entity Framework Core with SQL Server
  - Azure SQL Database for metadata, users, comments, subscriptions
  - FFmpeg for synchronous video transcoding during upload
  - Azure Blob Storage for originals and transcoded renditions
  - Azure CDN for global video delivery
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service for API hosting
  - Azure Redis Cache for hot video metadata and session tokens
  - Azure Service Bus for transcoding job queue
  - Single database with tables: Videos, Users, Comments, Subscriptions, WatchHistory, Playlists

data.text: Split into microservices by workload: Upload Service handles resumable chunked uploads, Transcoding Service processes videos into multiple renditions using a worker pool, Streaming Service serves HLS/DASH manifests and segments, Metadata Service manages search and recommendations, and Live Service handles RTMP/WHIP ingest and packaging.

items: Upload Service: Accepts chunked uploads with resumable protocol, computes checksums, stores raw files in blob storage, and emits VideoUploaded events for transcoding pipeline.

Transcoding Service: Consumes upload events, runs parallel FFmpeg jobs via Kubernetes or Azure Batch, generates HLS/DASH renditions at multiple bitrates, extracts thumbnails and captions, and publishes VideoReady events.
Streaming Service: Serves HLS/DASH manifests and video segments, manages signed URLs for protected content, supports multi-CDN failover, and handles live stream packaging (HLS/LL-HLS/DASH).
Metadata Service: Manages video titles, descriptions, tags, categories, and search indexing using Elasticsearch or Azure Cognitive Search, exposes gRPC for recommendation candidate retrieval.

Recommendation Service: Computes personalized video suggestions using collaborative filtering and deep learning models, ingests watch history and engagement events, and serves ranked candidates via low-latency API.
Live Service: Handles RTMP/WHIP ingest from broadcasters, transcodes live streams in real-time, manages live chat via WebSocket, and archives live recordings to blob storage.

    Video/

        VideoPlayer.tsx          # HLS.js with quality selector
        WatchPage.tsx            # Video + comments + suggestions
        UploadFlow.tsx            # Chunked upload with progress
        LiveStream.tsx            # Low-latency player + chat
        Transcript.tsx            # Closed captions overlay
        RecommendationRail.tsx    # Horizontal scroll suggestions
      hooks/
        useHlsPlayer.ts           # HLS.js + DASH.js integration
        useChunkedUpload.ts       # Resumable upload with retry
        useWatchHistory.ts        # Sync progress to backend
        useLiveChat.ts            # WebSocket chat consumer
      store/
        playerSlice.ts            # Playback state, quality, speed
        uploadSlice.ts            # Upload queue, progress
  shared/
    ui/
    lib/
    hooks/

Key Patterns:
  - HLS.js or Shaka Player for adaptive streaming
  - Service Worker for offline video caching
  - Web Worker for client-side video thumbnail generation
  - Intersection Observer for auto-pause offscreen videos
  - MediaSource Extensions for custom buffer management

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: Video platforms are storage and bandwidth intensive - use multi-CDN with origin shield
Transcoding is CPU-heavy and async - decouple upload from processing via queues
Adaptive streaming requires pre-generated renditions at multiple bitrates
Recommendations require separate feature stores and ML pipelines from the serving path
Live streaming needs real-time ingest, packaging, and sub-5s end-to-end latency
data.takeaway: YouTube is a media-heavy distributed system with heavy async processing. Separate upload, transcoding, and streaming into independent services, pre-compute recommendations offline, and use multi-CDN with origin shielding for global playback performance.
